genxml.title: Dallas DS1685/DS1687 real-time clock and battery-backed RAM (Octane and Octane2 system boards)
genxml.doc: The real-time clock and 242 bytes of battery-backed user RAM on the Octane and Octane2 system boards, reached through the IOC3's byte bus. The DS1687 is the same die in a package with its crystal and cell. The register contract here covers what the sources consulted state: the calendar and alarm bytes, the user RAM in its two banks, the bank-1 control and flag bytes that software polls, the extended-RAM ports and the identification bytes. Offsets are byte addresses within a bank. Register A to Register D are not listed: their bit meanings and offsets were not transcribed for this unit, and the bit positions of the bank-1 control bytes are not stated either. Grades say how each item was derived: established means the vendor datasheet text the sources quote, inferred means the public Linux or OpenBSD driver's use of the byte. None of it was measured on a board, and reset values are unknown unless a source states one.

struct.name: USER_RAM
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_nvram_write, which treats the bank-0 bytes as one 114-byte run
struct.doc: Bank-0 user RAM, 114 bytes. The driver's write loop covers a 50-byte run from 0Eh and a 64-byte run from 40h, whose sum is 114, so the block runs from 0Eh to 7Fh. The sources do not state a layout inside it; Linux exposes it as unstructured storage.

struct.name: MODEL
struct.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, silicon serial number section (page 18): register 40h holds the model number 71h, read-only
struct.doc: Model byte, the first of the eight identification bytes; the datasheet gives the value 71h. Probe does not read it, so only the sysfs and proc views show a wrong value.

struct.name: SERIAL
struct.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, silicon serial number section (page 18): registers 41h to 46h, unique and read-only
struct.doc: Six serial-number bytes that follow the model byte. Linux exposes them through sysfs and nothing consulted checks them.

struct.name: SERIAL_CRC
struct.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, silicon serial number section (page 18): register 47h, CRC over 40h to 46h
struct.doc: CRC byte over the seven identification bytes before it. The datasheet text gives no polynomial, so this import cannot reproduce the check. No driver consulted validates it.

struct.name: CENTURY
struct.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, century register section (bank 1, 48h, binary or BCD); Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time
struct.doc: Century, in the same data-mode form as the other calendar bytes. Linux computes the year as the year byte plus the century times 100.

struct.name: DATE_ALARM
struct.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet, wake-up section, as quoted by the sources consulted
struct.doc: Date alarm. The wake-up alarm matches this byte together with the hours, minutes and seconds alarm bytes. Linux also writes it as the alarm date.

struct.name: CTRL4A
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, probe and poweroff paths; OpenBSD power driver, power_intr
struct.doc: Extended control and flag byte. Only the bits named below are positioned here. Its other bits (the wake-up, RAM-clear and valid-battery flags) are read and cleared by the drivers, but their positions are not transcribed in this unit.

field.name: incr
field.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, which polls this bit without a bound before every access

field.name: pab
field.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet, power-control section, as quoted by the sources consulted

field.name: kickstart_flag
field.from: OpenBSD power driver and NetBSD ds1687 header, which name bit 0 of this byte as the kickstart flag

struct.name: CTRL4B
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, probe and remove paths
struct.doc: Extended enable byte, holding the enables for the wake-up, RAM-clear and kickstart interrupts. Linux writes it at probe and remove. Bit positions are not transcribed in this unit.

struct.name: EXT_RAM_ADDRESS
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, extended-RAM read and write paths; the vendor text as quoted by the sources
struct.doc: Address for the extended RAM, seven bits. The address does not advance on its own, so software writes it before each byte.

struct.name: EXT_RAM_DATA
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, extended-RAM read and write paths
struct.doc: Extended RAM data at the address in the address register.

struct.name: SECONDS
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time, which reads this byte first among the time fields
struct.doc: Seconds. Binary or BCD according to the data-mode bit, which this unit does not carry.

struct.name: ALARM_SECONDS
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, alarm read and write paths
struct.doc: Seconds alarm byte. Linux's alarm paths read and write it with the other alarm bytes; the sources consulted do not describe how the match treats a wildcard value.

struct.name: MINUTES
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time
struct.doc: Minutes. Same data-mode rule as seconds.

struct.name: ALARM_MINUTES
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, alarm read and write paths
struct.doc: Minutes alarm byte.

struct.name: HOURS
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time and its probe, which forces 24-hour mode
struct.doc: Hours. Linux forces 24-hour mode at probe and converts the stored value first if the chip was in 12-hour mode.

struct.name: ALARM_HOURS
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, probe conversion of both hours registers
struct.doc: Hours alarm byte. Probe converts it together with the time hours when it finds 12-hour mode.

struct.name: DAY_OF_WEEK
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time; OpenBSD dsrtc driver, ds1687_settime
struct.doc: Day of the week. Linux reads it on the time path and OpenBSD writes it on the set path; OpenBSD's read path does not read it.

struct.name: DATE
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time
struct.doc: Date of the month.

struct.name: MONTH
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time
struct.doc: Month.

struct.name: YEAR
struct.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_rtc_read_time
struct.doc: Year within the century. The century comes from the century byte in bank 1.

constant.name: BANK0_RAM_BYTES
constant.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver, ds1685_nvram_write bank-0 arithmetic

constant.name: EXT_RAM_BYTES
constant.from: Linux rtc-ds1685 driver; the extended address is seven bits

constant.name: RAM_CLEAR_RECOVERY_MS
constant.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, RAM clear section (page 20) and electrical characteristics (tREC 150 ms)

constant.name: RAM_TOTAL_BYTES
constant.from: Maxim DS1685 datasheet 19-5215 rev 10/12, features list and RAM clear section (page 20): 242 bytes
